MATHEMATICS, PH.D.
College of Arts and Sciences
Department: Mathematics and Statistics
Major Contacts, Deadlines, and Delivery Information
Concentrations:
Pure and Applied
Statistics
The Ph.D. in Mathematics provides the experience and knowledge to understand and appreciate prior accomplishments in the discipline and develops the skills necessary for a meaningful contribution to the intellectual advancement and applications of the discipline. It prepares its graduates to pursue long-term careers in their field by providing solid and cutting-edge knowledge. Graduates receive training that enables them to conduct independent research and write research papers publishable in peer-reviewed journals of their discipline, as well as a technical education enabling them to take on leading positions in a modern economy.
Major Research Areas
Algebra & Number Theory, Applied Statistics, Approximation Theory, Bio-Mathematics, Complex & Harmonic Analysis, Cyber-Security & Cryptography, Data Science, Differential Equations, Graph Theory & Combinatorics, Low-Dimensional Topology, Mathematics Education, Mathematical Physics, Operator Theory, Probability, Statistical Learning, Stochastic Processes & Modelling
ADMISSION INFORMATION
Must meet University Admission and English Proficiency requirements as well as requirements for admission to the major, listed below.
A degree from an accredited institution relevant to the prospective concentration. Either
a Master’s degree or equivalent in mathematical sciences/statistics or a related area; or
a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in mathematical sciences/statistics or related area with a strong record of undergraduate/graduate courses related to prospective concentration.
GRE General test is recommended but not required.
Applicants to the Major who wish to pursue the Pure and Applied Concentration should have had a strong performance in at least one of the following or equivalent courses : Bridge to Abstract Mathematics, Elementary Abstract Algebra or Intermediate Analysis I to be successful.
Three letters of recommendation (two of which should be from college level mathematics/statistics professors)
A completed departmental application form, including a statement of goals.
A completed departmental graduate teaching assistantship application form (if such a position is desired).
Applicants to the Ph.D. program may be offered admission to the M.A. program and move to the Ph.D. program after establishing a record of success in graduate courses. Graduate Teaching and Research Assistantships are available on a competitive basis. Contact the Department for recommended prerequisites for each concentration.
CURRICULUM REQUIREMENTS
Total Minimum Hours: 72 hours post-baccalaureate
Core Requirements – 4 Credit Hours
Additional Required Courses - 6 Credit Hours
Concentration – 24 Credit Hours minimum (24 for Pure and Applied; 33 for Statistics)
Electives - 13 Credit Hours minimum (22 for Pure and Applied; 13 for Statistics)
Dissertation – 10 Credit Hours minimum
Directed Research or Dissertation - 6 Credit Hours minimum
CORE REQUIREMENTS (4 CREDIT HOURS MINIMUM)
MAE 5177 Teaching College Mathematics Credit Hours: 3
MAT 5710 Scientific Computation and Writing Credit Hours: 1
ADDITIONAL REQUIRED COURSES (6 CREDIT HOURS)
MAA 5307 Real Analysis I Credit Hours: 3
MAS 5145 Advanced Linear Algebra Credit Hours: 3
CONCENTRATIONS
Students must select from one of the concentrations below. Each concentration offers coherent pairs/triples of courses, to ensure a certain breadth and depth of disciplinary knowledge.
PURE AND APPLIED CONCENTRATION (24 CREDIT HOURS)
Required Concentration Courses (9 credit hours):
MAS 5311 Algebra I Credit Hours: 3
MAA 6406 Complex Analysis I Credit Hours: 3
MTG 5316 Topology I Credit Hours: 3
FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE IN ALGEBRA, ANALYSIS OR TOPOLOGY (6 CREDIT HOURS MINIMUM)
Complete at least two of the following courses listed below with a 3.00 GPA average. Substitutions may be allowed with prior approval of both the Concentration Director and Concentration Graduate Committee:
MAS 6312 Algebra II Credit Hours: 3
OR
MAA 5306 Introduction to Real Analysis Credit Hours: 3
MAA 6616 Real Analysis II Credit Hours: 3
OR
MTG 6317 Topology II Credit Hours: 3
MATHEMATICS DEPTH (9 CREDIT HOURS MINIMUM)
Complete courses from at least two categories from the list below with at least a 3.00 GPA average. Substitutions may be allowed with prior approval of both the Concentration Director and Concentration Graduate Committee:
APPLIED ALGEBRA AND NUMBER THEORY (6 CREDIT HOURS)
MAS 6325 Applied Algebra Credit Hours: 3 AND
MAS 6220 Algebraic Number Theory Credit Hours: 3
APPLIED MATHEMATICS (9 CREDIT HOURS)
Select one course from each of the following course pairs:
MAP 5407 Methods of Applied Mathematics Credit Hours: 3 OR
MAP 5345 Applied Partial Differential Equations Credit Hours: 3
AND
MAA 5405 Applied Complex Analysis Credit Hours: 3 OR
MAD 6406 Numerical Linear Algebra Credit Hours: 3
AND
MAP 6205 Control Theory and Optimization Credit Hours: 3 OR
MAP 6312 Dynamical Systems I Credit Hours: 3
COMBINATORICS (6 CREDIT HOURS)
MAD 6206 Combinatorics I Credit Hours: 3 AND
MAD 6207 Combinatorics II Credit Hours: 3
COMPLEX ANALYSIS (3 CREDIT HOURS)
MAA 6407 Complex Analysis II Credit Hours: 3
DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS (6 CREDIT HOURS)
MAP 6312 Dynamical Systems I Credit Hours: 3 AND
MAP 6319 Dynamical Systems II Credit Hours: 3
FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS (6 CREDIT HOURS)
MAA 6506 Functional Analysis I Credit Hours: 3 AND
MAA 6507 Functional Analysis II Credit Hours: 3
GRAPH THEORY (6 CREDIT HOURS)
MAD 6305 Graph Theory I Credit Hours: 3 AND
MAD 6308 Graph Theory II Credit Hours: 3
HARMONIC ANALYSIS (6 CREDIT HOURS)
MAP 6418 Harmonic Analysis Credit Hours: 3 AND
MAP 6356 Partial Differential Equations Credit Hours: 3
NONLINEAR ANALYSIS (6 CREDIT HOURS)
MAP 5316 Ordinary Differential Equations I Credit Hours: 3 AND
MAP 5317 Ordinary Differential Equations II Credit Hours: 3
PARTIAL DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS (6 CREDIT HOURS)
MAP 5345 Applied Partial Differential Equations Credit Hours: 3 AND
MAP 6356 Partial Differential Equations Credit Hours: 3
THEORY OF COMPUTING (6 CREDIT HOURS)
MAD 6616 Algebraic Automata Theory Credit Hours: 3 AND
MAD 6510 Algorithms in Discrete Structures Credit Hours: 3
OTHER COURSE OPTIONS (6 CREDIT HOURS)
Two courses selected from the standard graduate-level courses or MAT 6932 Selected Topics, subject to the approval of the Graduate Director and the Graduate Committee. Credit Hours: 6
STATISTICS CONCENTRATION (33 CREDIT HOURS MINIMUM)
Required Concentration Courses (15 credit hours):
STA 5446 Probability Theory I Credit Hours: 3
STA 6447 Probability Theory II Credit Hours: 3
STA 5526 Non-Parametric Statistics Credit Hours: 3
STA 6205 Design of Experiments Credit Hours: 3
STA 6746 Multivariate Analysis Credit Hours: 3
FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE IN STATISTICAL METHODS AND MATHEMATICAL STATISTICS (15 CREDIT HOURS):
Complete the following courses listed below with a 3.00 GPA average. Substitutions may be allowed with prior approval of both the Concentration Director and Concentration Graduate Committee:
Statistical Methods (9 credit hours):
STA 5166 Statistical Methods I Credit Hours: 3 AND
STA 6167 Statistical Methods II Credit Hours: 3 AND
STA 6208 Linear Statistical Models Credit Hours: 3
Mathematical Statistics (6 credit hours):
STA 5326 Mathematical Statistics I Credit Hours: 3 AND
STA 6348 Mathematical Statistics II Credit Hours: 3
STATISTICAL DEPTH (3 CREDIT HOURS MINIMUM):
Complete courses from at least one category from the list below with at least a 3.00 GPA average. Substitutions may be allowed with prior approval of both the Concentration Director and Concentration Graduate Committee.
LINEAR MODELS AND MULTIVARIATE ANALYSIS (3 CREDIT HOURS):
STA 6703 Statistical Learning Theory and Applications Credit Hours: 3
INDUSTRIAL STATISTICS (3 CREDIT HOURS):
STA 5676 Reliability Data Analysis Credit Hours: 3
STOCHASTIC PROCESSES AND TIME SERIES ANALYSIS (10 CREDIT HOURS):
STA 6876 Time Series Analysis Credit Hours: 3
STA 6206 Stochastic Processes Credit Hours: 3
MAT 6932 Selected Topics Credit Hours: 1-4 taken as Stochastic Modelling of Dynamical Systems (4 Credit hours for this program)
ELECTIVES (13 CREDIT HOURS MINIMUM*)
Students select additional graduate courses to enhance their depth in math or statistics in consultation with their Concentration Director, to meet minimum hours for the Major.
*students in the Pure and Applied Concentration need to take 22 credit hours minimum to meet the total minimum of 72 hours required for this degree.
QUALIFYING EXAMINATIONS
The student is required to pass two Fundamental Qualifying Examinations at the Ph.D. level, which are based on their elective choices. For each subject, the exam may be attempted twice. A third attempt in a subject may be permitted with the approval of the Graduate Committee and Graduate Director. After passing two Fundamental Qualifying Examinations, the student will select a Dissertation Advisor, who will convene a Specialty Examination Committee to author a Specialty Examination. Passing two Fundamental Qualifying Examinations and the Specialty Examination at the Ph.D. level is considered passing the Doctoral Qualifying Examination.
DIRECTED RESEARCH OR DISSERTATION (6 CREDIT HOURS MINIMUM)
Students admitted to doctoral candidacy are required to take at least 10 hours in MAT 7980 Dissertation: Doctoral, and at least 6 combined hours of MAT 7980 and MAT 7912. For the Directed Research hours to be counted, it must be approved by the Major Advisor and the Program Director.
MAT 7980 Dissertation: Doctoral Credit Hours: 2-19 (0-6 Credit Hours), in addition to the 10 hours (see below in Dissertation)
MAT 7912 Directed Research Credit Hours: 1-19 (0-6 Credit Hours)
DISSERTATION (10 CREDIT HOURS MINIMUM)
The candidate will conduct original and significant research which is worthy of publication. The research will be described in the doctoral dissertation. Research towards the dissertation typically forms the major part of the work required for the Ph.D. in Mathematics. The Doctoral Dissertation Defense shall consist of an oral presentation of the research in the dissertation to the supervisory committee.
MAT 7980 Dissertation: Doctoral Credit Hours: 2-19 (10 credit hours minimum for this program)
PROGRAM HANDBOOK
The student is responsible for familiarizing themselves with the additional program requirements and expectations listed in the program handbook, particularly those concerning timely progress. Handbook: https://www.usf.edu/arts-sciences/departments/mathematics-statistics/graduate/advising-and-forms.aspx
